answer: Each agent can earn influence only after completing a sequence of tasks whose outputs are checked against hidden, randomly assigned test cases, with rewards released gradually as later work confirms earlier results. A vertex in the trust graph gains weight from verified history, not from a claimed identity; an atlas of task dependencies helps spot duplicated outputs, while glacier-paced vesting prevents a fresh account from cashing out immediately. A sybil attacker must therefore reproduce useful work across many accounts and wait, tying up compute and capital for uncertain returns.
